purpose: Close the Docker gap: the images were built at research-v1 and not rebuilt for R3/R4.
baseline_before: No stack was running and the existing images were two days old (pre-R3/R4); frontend/dist was stale. There was nothing to smoke-test, so the first smoke run is on the rebuilt stack.

build.command: docker compose down -v --remove-orphans; docker compose build --no-cache; docker compose up -d
build.source: official from-scratch build (docker/api.Dockerfile, docker/web.Dockerfile); the registry was reachable, so the offline overlay build was not used
build.r3r4_code_in_image: backend.correlation.explain has 'observation' (checked inside the built api image)
build.containers: redis, api, web all healthy; clean volumes (no data carried over)

checks: strict CSP and security headers; nginx version hidden; SPA fallback
API reachable only through the proxy, auth enforced
client address cannot be spoofed to dodge the failed-key limiter
explicit availability across the proxy (null group 202, half-missing 422, omitted field 422)
WebSocket works through nginx, tokens not in logs

observation_check.note: First attempt failed at the spike step because the synthetic device was still learning after 800 events (the unfamiliar-endpoint baseline needs 3600 s of event time plus 720 samples, about 1440 events); alerts are withheld while learning. A test-design error, not a runtime defect: the script now warms until the device reports learning=False (it did at 1500 events) and uses a fresh device id. No detector, model or threshold was changed.

checks.check: empty, unknown and repeated declarations are rejected (422)
declared signals=['network'] is stored and returned by GET /devices and /devices/{id}
observability full, state normal, unsupported = device+proximity+spatial, nothing missing or recovering
location sent by a device that never declared it is treated as unsupported (state unchanged)
alert record: unsupported = device+proximity+spatial; text: The location, device-health and proximity signals are not supported by this device. This a...
network lost: state degraded, missing = ['network'], observability blind

alert.observation: The location, device-health and proximity signals are not supported by this device. This alert is based on network telemetry only. Signals that were not observed neither confirm nor rule out an attack.

dashboard_e2e.detail: login, calibration, intrusion alert raised and closed, signal loss shown as Degraded, device network, anomalies, statistics, evidence, reload keeps session, viewer without controls, phone width with 0 px horizontal overflow; no failed HTTP responses, no browser errors

demo_story.detail: seven scenes asserted; docs/img/demo screenshots regenerated from the rebuilt stack

alerts_seen_in_stack: demo intrusion alert: observation "All four signals were observed."; network-only device alert: unsupported device+proximity+spatial, text states it rests on network telemetry only
frozen_artifacts: unchanged: no file under models/, docs/research/ or any frozen manifest was edited; tests/test_frozen_artifact.py passes
not_covered: TLS, key rotation, per-user accounts, multi-node (unchanged limits)
pixel-exact reproducibility of the demo screenshots

after a restart, an incoming event from a declared device was not re-sent (its device key was not kept); the in-memory declaration map is rebuilt from the store at start-up and covered by the store-level tests

persistence_across_full_restart.command: docker compose down; docker compose up -d (volumes kept)
persistence_across_full_restart.result: all three containers healthy again; GET /devices still returns signals=["network"] for the two declared test devices; the network-only device's alert (unsupported = device, proximity, spatial) is still in the store

supersedes: the Docker limitation recorded in docs/results/r3r4_release.json (frozen, not edited)

ui_clarity_revision.trigger: review of the demo screenshots: a device at 0.89 labelled Low while the text said all four signals were normal; the same explanation shown twice on the alert detail; unclear what the score and the labels mean
ui_clarity_revision.verification_of_labels: not a backend or mapping bug: the frozen bands (Low from 0.452, Medium from 0.903, High from 0.983) classify 0.89 as Low. The presentation was misleading: ring and sentence looked only at per-signal active levels (0.30), while the learned, saturating fusion can put weak signals into a non-normal band
changes: ring and sentence now say "LOW · COMBINED" / "No single signal is active (0.30+), yet together the fused risk is X: Low band, alert level Y." instead of NOMINAL / "all four signals are normal" when the severity is not Normal

collapsible "How to read this score": instantaneous per-update score with a 1 s half-life hold, the band thresholds, a learned saturating scale and not a probability, alert opens at the alert level once the device has finished learning and closes after 60 s below the clear level (so a device can read Normal while its alert is open)
alert detail leads with "What this alert rests on" (the R4 observation sentence) and collapses the repeated technical explanation under "Full technical explanation"
ui_clarity_revision.no_change_to: backend, detectors, models, thresholds, severity bands, research artifacts
ui_clarity_revision.tests: frontend 66 passed (62 + 4 new), tsc clean; web image rebuilt; e2e_dashboard E2E OK; demo_story DEMO STORY OK
ui_clarity_revision.demo_story_flake: one run failed at scene 1 because the live simulated fleet had D-005 in the Low band (0.49) for a few seconds when the script asserted Normal; not reproduced in 5 later runs; the script now waits up to a minute for Normal before asserting
